Pooled result

HR 0.8655 (0.7877 to 0.951), 95% interval

First occurrence of the composite of cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, non-fatal stroke, or hospitalisation for heart failure. random, estimator REML, k = 2.

τ² 0 · I² 0% · Q 0.01432 on 1 df

Favours: the intervention (lower is better)

Q = 0.0143 on 1 df: the two trials agree closely, which is what the same endpoint in one programme should look like.

Both trials report the same composite with the same four components in the same order, in CKD with type 2 diabetes, against placebo. Q = 0.0143 on 1 df.

Read this beside the estimate. FIDELIO-DKD (NCT02540993) registers the kidney composite as its primary outcome and the cardiovascular composite -- the one pooled here -- as the first of five secondaries. FIGARO-DKD (NCT02545049) registers them the other way round. The quantity is identical on both, word for word, so this is a question about which rank was selected and not about what was measured.

The unadjusted interval is HR 0.8655 (0.7877 to 0.9510) and excludes no effect. This project's floored Hartung-Knapp interval at k = 2 is 0.4699 to 1.5940 and includes it. At k = 2 the t critical value is 12.7062 and almost nothing survives, so this is weaker evidence against the result than the same crossing would be at larger k. Note that metafor's RAW interval here, 0.8045 to 0.9311, is narrower than the unadjusted one -- which is what the house floor exists to prevent, and it is not cited as ours.

Does the answer depend on the pooling method?

With two or three studies the Cochrane Handbook (10.10.4.4–10.10.4.5) asks for a sensitivity analysis comparing interval methods rather than a choice between them. Both are given here; the published interval is the first row.

Table 8. Does the answer depend on the pooling method?
IntervalMethodSummary (95% CI)
as publishedREML0.8655 (0.7877 to 0.951)
sensitivity (Handbook 10.10.4.5)REML with Hartung-Knapp, t on k-1 = 1 degree(s) of freedom (t = 12.7062)0.8655 (0.4699 to 1.594)

The published point is 0.8655 and the house-rule point is 0.8655. The number a reader remembers does not move; what differs is the precision claim. That is why nothing downstream catches this -- every memorable quantity survives.

A floor of 1 is applied to the variance-inflation factor so the adjustment can never narrow an interval below the unadjusted one. That guard is the recognised modification for exactly this instability, and its existence is evidence the small-k behaviour is a known problem with known handling rather than a novel judgement.

Scopecomposite of cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, non-fatal stroke or hospitalisation for heart failure -- the same composite this object pools
The finding of this comparisonThis is the control case for class 76 and it was predicted before the screen ran. Four topics have now been found where the published synthesis chose a better-defined target than this corpus did. Here it did not: an aggregate-data pool of two trials reproduces a prespecified individual-patient-data analysis of the same two trials to three significant figures. The pool was feasible -- one drug, one programme, complementary populations by design, pooling prespecified by the trialists -- and where the pool is feasible the method holds. That makes class 76 a finding about feasibility rather than about arithmetic, and it is the reason a pattern needs a case where it does not fire.
What is not establishedThe concealment mechanism is not on the registry and no publication was read.
Why this is not an adjudicated disputeA blind second assessor from a different model family disagreed with this domain on 89% of judgements across 22 topics. That would ordinarily be a dispute to adjudicate. It is not one: the tool's own text names this exact evidential situation -- a bare statement that a study was randomised -- and prescribes the answer. The second assessor is not being deferred to; the guidance is being applied.
What the registry gives and does notA ClinicalTrials.gov design module records `allocation: Randomized`. It carries no sequence-generation method and no allocation-concealment mechanism. The original judgement's own note said so before scoring LOW.
How this maps to the tool s algorithmThe tool maps 'No information' on 1.1 and 1.2 with no baseline concern to a domain judgement of some concerns. This project writes no information on the domain when it could not be judged from the sources read, and caps the overall at some concerns. Same place, and it keeps 'we could not judge this' distinguishable from 'we judged it and had concerns'.
What does not changeNo overall rating and no GRADE CERTAINTY moves. All 51 judgements were already capped at some concerns or HIGH by another no information domain.
The two trials register the same two composites with the ranks swappedFIDELIO-DKD registers the kidney composite as its primary and the cardiovascular composite as its first secondary. FIGARO-DKD registers the cardiovascular composite as its primary and the kidney composite as its first secondary. This review pools the cardiovascular composite, so it takes one trial's primary and the other's secondary -- and the quantity is identical, word for word, on both registrations.
Corpus exposure if assessor 2 is right on the randomisation process84 the randomisation process judgements exist across this corpus and 51 are scored LOW, over 15 topics. Every one rests on the same evidence -- the registry recording an allocation of randomized -- and every one sits beside a note saying the concealment mechanism was not read. If the second assessor is right, 51 judgements and the overall rating above each of them are wrong in the direction that flatters the trials. Changing them is a methodological decision and it is not made here.
What is not claimedThat this reconciliation completes the limb. One topic of at least fifteen has a second assessment. `rob2.assessors` remains deliberately unwritten on every object including this one.
And it bounds a finding of oursClass 94 records assessor 2 saying no information on the randomisation process/deviations from the intended intervention/missing outcome data `100 of 100`. Measured across all 23 topics now stored that is 239 of 243, and all four exceptions are the randomisation process=some concerns on `agyw-hiv-prep-review` and `cab-prep-hiv-review` -- two of the three topics asked under the earlier prompt build, the one whose reply ids are bare NCTs. Under that build it is 4 of 6; under the later build 0 of 75. The 100% was measured on the later build's topics. The two-defaults mechanism stands; its universality does not, and what varies with it is the prompt.
The rate is still conditional on the same allow listBoth numbers are conditional on the fact list in THE_ALLOW_LIST_THE_RATE_IS_CONDITIONAL_ON above. Neither is a rate of agreement between assessors in general.
Which risk of bias domains drove the ratingWhere a result is rated worse than LOW overall, the domain carrying that judgement is: selection of the reported result on 1 result(s). The overall rating is the worst domain, so these are the domains that determine it.

Title and review question

Finerenone against placebo in chronic kidney disease with type 2 diabetes: the cardiovascular composite, pooled from the two pivotal trials1

Two trial acronyms were transposed and are corrected. This object recorded NCT02545049 as FIDELIO-DKD. It is figaro-dkd. Read from ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 on 2026-08-21: NCT02540993 carries acronym FIDELIO-DKD, NCT02545049 carries acronym FIGARO-DKD. The two trials differ in their registered primary -- FIDELIO-DKD's is the kidney composite, FIGARO-DKD's the cardiovascular one -- so naming them the wrong way round is not a typographical matter: it attributes each trial's design to the other. No estimate moves; the estimates were keyed to the registration numbers, which were right throughout. 2 label(s) corrected.2

In adults with chronic kidney disease and type 2 diabetes, does finerenone reduce the first occurrence of the composite of cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, non-fatal stroke, or hospitalisation for heart failure, against placebo?3

Abstract

Question. In adults with chronic kidney disease and type 2 diabetes, does finerenone reduce the first occurrence of the composite of cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, non-fatal stroke, or hospitalisation for heart failure, against placebo?1

Methods. estimates were pooled under a random-effects model with the REML estimator; risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 (Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials); and certainty was rated with GRADE, following the Cochrane Handbook chapter 14. Randomised evidence starts HIGH and is rated down with reasons.2

Results. First occurrence of the composite of cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, non-fatal stroke, or hospitalisation for heart failure: hazard ratio 0.866 (0.788 to 0.951) across 2 trials; 1 of these pooled outcome(s) carries a stated qualification -- a referral or a recorded finding -- given in full in Results and not reproduced here; the trials agreed closely (I-squared 0%); and certainty of the evidence was moderate.3

Introduction

1Background. This review asks: In adults with chronic kidney disease and type 2 diabetes, does finerenone reduce the first occurrence of the composite of cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, non-fatal stroke, or hospitalisation for heart failure, against placebo? It pools 2 randomised trials, against placebo. The outcome pooled is First occurrence of the composite of cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, non-fatal stroke, or hospitalisation for heart failure.

[Draft] The evidence identified on this question is 2 randomised trials (NCT02540993, NCT02545049), pooled here at 0.866 (95% CI 0.788 to 0.951) for cv_composite_first. Certainty in that estimate is rated MODERATE, rated down for risk of bias, inconsistency and indirectness. Which of those unresolved points makes the question worth asking now is the author's judgement.2

[Draft] A search for published syntheses matched 252 record(s); 252 were read and 1 appraised against this review. The appraised synthesis is Cardiovascular and kidney outcomes with finerenone in patients with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease: the FIDELITY pooled analysis (European Heart Journal, 2022). Whether those differences warrant a new synthesis rather than citing the existing one is the author's judgement.3

Methods — synthesis

For first occurrence of the composite of cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, non-fatal stroke, or hospitalisation for heart failure, a random model was fitted with the REML estimator.1

Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 (Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials) (), following . 2 result-level assessments were made.2

A ceiling applies to every risk-of-bias judgement in this review; it is stated with the assessment itself rather than summarised here.3

Certainty of evidence was rated with GRADE, following the Cochrane Handbook chapter 14. Randomised evidence starts HIGH and is rated down with reasons., following . 0 pooled outcome(s) were rated. 1 outcome(s) were not rated because their pool is declined or withdrawn: there is no effect estimate to rate the certainty of, and rating one would be certainty about a number this review refused to publish.4

Results

The pooled hazard ratio for first occurrence of the composite of cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, non-fatal stroke, or hospitalisation for heart failure was 0.866 (0.788 to 0.951) across 2 trials, against placebo.1

Noted on this pool. Read this beside the estimate. FIDELIO-DKD (NCT02540993) registers the kidney composite as its primary outcome and the cardiovascular composite -- the one pooled here -- as the first of five secondaries. FIGARO-DKD (NCT02545049) registers them the other way round. The quantity is identical on both, word for word, so this is a question about which rank was selected and not about what was measured. The unadjusted interval is HR 0.8655 (0.7877 to 0.9510) and excludes no effect. This project's floored Hartung-Knapp interval at k = 2 is 0.4699 to 1.5940 and includes it. At k = 2 the t critical value is 12.7062 and almost nothing survives, so this is weaker evidence against the result than the same crossing would be at larger k. Note that metafor's RAW interval here, 0.8045 to 0.9311, is narrower than the unadjusted one -- which is what the house floor exists to prevent, and it is not cited as ours.2

The trials' results were closely consistent with one another: I-squared, the share of the variation between them that is more than chance alone would produce, was 0%; the estimated variance of the true effects between trials (tau-squared) was 0, the heterogeneity test statistic Q was 0.0143, on degrees of freedom 1. Q = 0.0143 on 1 df: the two trials agree closely, which is what the same endpoint in one programme should look like.3

The grounds for pooling are recorded as: Both trials report the same composite with the same four components in the same order, in CKD with type 2 diabetes, against placebo. Q = 0.0143 on 1 df. Where a later pool on this page rests on the same grounds, they are not restated.4

The full model output for every pooled outcome -- the call, the estimator, the heterogeneity statistics and the back-transformed interval -- is reproduced verbatim as Extended data at the end of this article, so every number above can be checked against the software that produced it.5

Risk of bias in the included results

Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 (Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials). The unit of assessment is a result1

A domain that cannot be judged from the sources read is no information, never LOW. Low-by-default asserts a fact; high-by-default invents a defect. Overall is capped at some concerns wherever a domain is no information.2

A second, independent assessment was obtained from: gpt-5 Codex (openai family), via `codex exec`, model self-named in the same session3

The assessment above was made by: Claude Opus 5 (anthropic family)4

How the second assessor was asked: Blind. The second assessor was given the registration facts and the house NO_INFORMATION-never-LOW rule inline, and asked to score the five domains and an overall for each result. It was not shown this assessment and was not asked whether it agreed. Asking 'do you agree' measures deference, not judgement.5

The disagreement rate, reported as disagreement because agreement between two assessors given the same facts authenticates nothing: 5 of 12 judgements -- 41.7%. Reported as disagreement and not as agreement: agreement between two assessors given the same facts authenticates nothing, and the whole value of a second assessor is in what it does not confirm.6

Where they disagree, by domain: the randomisation process 2 of 2 disagree, deviations from the intended intervention 0 of 2 disagree, missing outcome data 0 of 2 disagree, measurement of the outcome 0 of 2 disagree, selection of the reported result 1 of 2 disagree and overall 2 of 2 disagree.7

That rate was measured before this review's the randomisation process judgements moved. It is left as measured: On 2026-08-21 this review's the randomisation process judgements moved from LOW to no information on the RoB 2 guidance -- the position assessor 2 had taken. The rate above was measured before that and is left exactly as measured: it is a published number, it is the record of what a blind second assessor said, and it is the reason the guidance was re-read. Editing it would delete the evidence that the change was warranted. This is the same computation re-run on the object as it now stands, so both are visible and neither is silently corrected.8

Re-run on the object as it now stands: 3 of 12 judgements -- 25.0%. By domain: the randomisation process 0 of 2 disagree, deviations from the intended intervention 0 of 2 disagree, missing outcome data 0 of 2 disagree, measurement of the outcome 0 of 2 disagree, selection of the reported result 1 of 2 disagree and overall 2 of 2 disagree.9

2 the randomisation process judgement(s) on this topic moved. Any the randomisation process disagreement that remains is one where this assessment said some concerns rather than LOW -- assessor 2 said no information there too, and the guidance applied here speaks to LOW, not to some concerns. So a claim that 'the the randomisation process disagreement is resolved' would be false wherever those two numbers differ, which is why the count is re-run per topic instead of asserted once.10

the randomisation process now agrees with assessor 2 on every compared result.11

Class 94 records assessor 2 saying no information on the randomisation process/deviations from the intended intervention/missing outcome data `100 of 100`. Measured across all 23 topics now stored that is 239 of 243, and all four exceptions are the randomisation process=some concerns on `agyw-hiv-prep-review` and `cab-prep-hiv-review` -- two of the three topics asked under the earlier prompt build, the one whose reply ids are bare NCTs. Under that build it is 4 of 6; under the later build 0 of 75. The 100% was measured on the later build's topics. The two-defaults mechanism stands; its universality does not, and what varies with it is the prompt.12

Disagreement -- the randomisation process on both results: Assessor 1 said LOW, assessor 2 said no information -- and assessor 2 has the better of it against assessor 1's own stated rule. RoB 2 domain 1 asks about the randomisation process: sequence generation, allocation concealment, and baseline imbalance. The registry records only that the design was randomized. Assessor 1's own the randomisation process entry says in its own words that 'the concealment mechanism is not on the registry and no publication was read' -- and then scores LOW, against this object's own ceiling, which says a domain that cannot be judged from the sources read is no information, never LOW. That is the low-by-default failure the ceiling exists to forbid, committed systematically.13

Disagreement -- selection of the reported result on NCT02540993: Assessor 1 said some concerns, assessor 2 said LOW. Genuinely contestable and not resolved here. Assessor 1 scored the pooled result being FIDELIO's registered secondary rather than its primary. Assessor 2's implicit position is the defensible counter-argument: RoB 2 domain 5 concerns selection among multiple measurements or analyses of the outcome being assessed, and which outcome a review chooses to review is not a bias in the trial. Left as a disagreement.14

Disagreement -- overall on both: A consequence of the the randomisation process disagreement, not an independent one.15

Risk of bias was assessed independently a second time by GPT-5 Codex (openai family), via `codex exec`, model self-named in the same session, blind to this assessment and given the same registry facts. 5 of 12 judgements -- 41.7%. Reported as disagreement and not as agreement: agreement between two assessors given the same facts authenticates nothing, and the whole value of a second assessor is in what it does not confirm. By domain: the randomisation process 2 of 2 disagree, deviations from the intended intervention 0 of 2 disagree, missing outcome data 0 of 2 disagree, measurement of the outcome 0 of 2 disagree, selection of the reported result 1 of 2 disagree, overall 2 of 2 disagree. Recounted after this review's the randomisation process judgements moved: 3 of 12 judgements -- 25.0%.16

Certainty of the evidence

Certainty was rated with GRADE, following the Cochrane Handbook chapter 14. Randomised evidence starts HIGH and is rated down with reasons..1

MODERATE certainty. The two trials agree almost exactly, both are quadruple-masked, and the pooled composite is defined identically on both registrations -- so the single downgrade is for the unread deviation and missing-data domains and for the pooled result being FIDELIO's registered secondary rather than its primary.2

Where a result is rated worse than LOW overall, the domain carrying that judgement is: selection of the reported result on 1 result(s). The overall rating is the worst domain, so these are the domains that determine it.3

Discussion

[Draft] The pooled HR is 0.866 (95% CI 0.788 to 0.951) over 2 trials. Certainty is rated MODERATE. Every contributing interval excludes no effect. Whether a change of that magnitude is clinically meaningful in this population is the author's judgement: no field on this object records a threshold of importance, and none is assumed here.1

[Draft] Across 2 trials, tau-squared 0; every trial interval excludes no effect. Whether that degree of disagreement matters clinically -- whether the trials are answering the same question in the same patients -- is the author's judgement.2

[Draft] This review pools 0.866 (95% CI 0.788 to 0.951) over 2 trials. The appraised synthesis pooled composite of cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, non-fatal stroke or hospitalisation for heart failure -- the same composite this object pools over 13,026 participants. Which trials that synthesis carries: Both contributing trials are keyed to verified registrations -- NCT02540993 (FIGARO-DKD) and NCT02545049 (FIDELIO-DKD) -- and the appraised analysis names both trials in its author line ('FIDELIO-DKD and FIGARO-DKD investigators') and its abstract. The trial-set match is read, not inferred from arithmetic. Why the two results differ -- whether by population, outcome definition, model or included set -- is the author's judgement.3

[Draft] The evidence base is 2 trials, assessed for risk of bias as some concerns on 2 result(s). GRADE certainty is MODERATE, rated down for risk of bias, inconsistency and indirectness. Whether that is enough to answer the question depends on the decision the answer is for, which is not stated on this object, and is the author's judgement.4

Comparison with published syntheses

Published syntheses were identified as follows. PubMed E-utilities, executed 2026-08-20. Query, counts and per-record disposition in ssot/finerenone-cv/appraisal/the screen of published syntheses.json.1

This review was compared against 1 published synthesis(es); the denominator is stated because a comparison against an unstated number of reviews is not a comparison.2

What this comparison found. This is the control case for class 76 and it was predicted before the screen ran. Four topics have now been found where the published synthesis chose a better-defined target than this corpus did. Here it did not: an aggregate-data pool of two trials reproduces a prespecified individual-patient-data analysis of the same two trials to three significant figures. The pool was feasible -- one drug, one programme, complementary populations by design, pooling prespecified by the trialists -- and where the pool is feasible the method holds. That makes class 76 a finding about feasibility rather than about arithmetic, and it is the reason a pattern needs a case where it does not fire.3

On what basis their trial set is known: Both contributing trials are keyed to verified registrations -- NCT02540993 (FIGARO-DKD) and NCT02545049 (FIDELIO-DKD) -- and the appraised analysis names both trials in its author line ('FIDELIO-DKD and FIGARO-DKD investigators') and its abstract. The trial-set match is read, not inferred from arithmetic.4

Notes on this record — sections not written, and why

Of the four properties this project requires of a completed topic, 4 are held (the number of published syntheses this review was compared against, a GRADE certainty rating for each pooled outcome, the statistical model's output, quoted as it was produced, a risk-of-bias judgement for each reported result).1
